assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based drugs opened a new therapeutic class for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large outcome benefits that extend to cardiovascular and renal disease. The path from peptide biology to durable long-acting agonists is clear and the clinical and societal impact is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and incretin effect in humans) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, intestinotropic and metabolic actions) are core. Knudsen is decisive for translating GLP-1 into long-acting drugs (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's early peptide characterization is a real credit question; the three-person limit forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of clinical use, large independent trials and consistent replication. Timing is right given the ongoing public-health impact.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener, Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is contested and I have not independently verified the details.
Whether the committee prefers the basic physiology or the drug-development strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, a conceptually new class of living drugs, with several approved products and a strong follow-on pipeline.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 costimulation and early design), June (4-1BB constructs and the first clinical successes in leukemia) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and TIL/gene-engineered T-cell pioneering) form a plausible trio. Eshhar and others outside the supplied credit are not available to us.
assessment.maturity: Strong clinical confirmation across centres and products; long-term follow-up now supports durability for a subset of patients. Solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity remain limits but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Credit boundaries between design principle and clinical translation are debated.
Long-term safety, including secondary T-cell malignancies, is still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision. It has transformed circuit analysis across species and began to enter therapeutic use, notably vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterized channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth (and Boyden) built the neuronal toolkit and demonstrated behavioural control. Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck have strong claims, so any three-person split leaves out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated, standard technique for two decades; recognition is timely. Clinical impact is still early, so the case rests on the research tool.
uncertainties: Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit; the fair split is unresolved.
Whether a methods advance with mainly research-tool impact fits the physiology or medicine criterion as strongly as a therapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a lethal infant disease into a treatable one. This is a clear mechanism-to-cure example and validated a platform for RNA therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ISS-N1 target; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis. The pair is a natural, compact configuration. Other contributors to SMA genetics (Melki, Lefebvre) lie outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with extensive real-world follow-up and independent trials; timely given broader antisense and RNA drug uptake.
uncertainties: Gene-replacement and small-molecule SMA therapies complicate the story of what is uniquely attributable.
Whether upstream SMN gene discovery should be recognized separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines are a rare case of cancer prevention at population scale, with demonstrated near elimination of high-grade cervical lesions and falling cervical cancer incidence in vaccinated cohorts.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP vaccine development, with Zhou) are the central names. Other groups (Kirnbauer, Rose, Zhou) have credit claims that make the allocation arguable.
assessment.maturity: Very mature with real-world effectiveness data across countries. Prior recognition of HPV as cause of cervical cancer (2008) does not preclude this vaccine step.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first made immunogenic VLPs.
Possible overlap in the committee's view with the earlier HPV recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, transforming chronic myeloid leukemia into a manageable chronic condition and showing the value of oncogene-directed drugs.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical proof of concept and leadership), Lydon (discovery of the compound at Ciba-Geigy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and follow-on inhibitors) are a coherent trio. Janet Rowley and others earlier established the underlying biology and are outside this credit.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with long-term survival data and wide replication. Recognition would be somewhat late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Chemistry contributions (Zimmermann and others) are not in the credited names.
Some members may see the underlying cancer genetics as the more fundamental step.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified a neuropeptide system essential for stable wakefulness and showed loss of orexin neurons underlies narcolepsy type 1, a clear mechanistic insight that has led to orexin receptor antagonists and agonist programmes.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa discovered orexins and their receptors; de Lecea and Kilduff independently found hypocretins; Mignot's canine genetics identified the hypocretin receptor 2 mutation. The competing, near-simultaneous discoveries make a three-person choice difficult.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed through human pathology and drugs (suvorexant); orexin agonists are in late clinical development, so the therapeutic arc is still maturing.
uncertainties: Priority dispute between the two original discovery groups.
Agonist therapy for narcolepsy is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-organizing adult stem-cell derived organoids from Lgr5+ cells created a general platform for modelling human tissue, disease, and personalized drug testing, with wide adoption across fields.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell identification and organoid culture work, with Sato as first author on the key intestinal organoid papers. A two-person configuration is clean, though the pluripotent-stem-cell organoid field has other contributors.
assessment.maturity: Technique is widely replicated and standard; clinical translation (regenerative and diagnostic use) is still emerging, which makes the medical impact more prospective than realized.
uncertainties: Whether the impact is mostly a research tool.
Overlap with other organoid and stem-cell traditions in credit.
